title: Every Reason Lions Think Twice About a 9 kg Honey Badger
alt_titles: Every Reason Six Lions Lost Interest in One Honey Badger
Every Reason Lions Think Twice Before Killing a Honey Badger
Why Even Lions Think Twice About a 9 kg Honey Badger
The 9 kg Animal Lions Would Rather Not Fight
thumbnail_brief: A huge male lion fills the left two-thirds leaning back with one paw lifted, unimpressed, a small honey badger stands its ground on the right with its white back stripe clear, and tiny Doug hides behind the badger with his red cap visible, with the words TOO MUCH WORK, so the title gives the reasons and the badger's 9 kg and the thumbnail gives the lion's verdict; no blood, no wounds, no snarling gore mouths, no cute cartoon faces, and no LION, BADGER, 9 KG or TWICE on the image. Variant B: six crude lions across a dirt road looking at each other as one honey badger runs straight at them, Doug behind it, IT CHARGED. Variant C: a lion holding the badger by its loose scruff as it turns round inside its skin to face the lion (no bite shown), Doug holding a HOW TO HOLD A BADGER card, IT BITES BACK.
description:
Lions can kill a honey badger, but a 9 kg badger with loose skin, a bite and a stink gives them every reason to think twice. Doug follows the honey badger from a puff adder bite to a beekeeper's hive, a leopard's tree and finally six lions on a road in South Africa.

Where should we send Doug next? Tell us in the comments.
Subscribe and watch Doug's death counter keep climbing.

van der Wal et al. (2023), Journal of Zoology, do honey badgers and honeyguides really cooperate: https://research-portal.uea.ac.uk/en/publications/do-honey-badgers-and-greater-honeyguide-birds-cooperate-to-access/

Kapama Ranger Blog (2012), one honey badger and six lions: http://web.archive.org/web/20260114103106/https://kapama.com/rangerblog/the-fearless-honey-badger/
